To summarize the facts –

According to the official Canadian statistics:

  1. " The average THC content of all samples analysed since 1995 is about 6%. "

  2. " Overall less than 10 % of all marihuana seized in Canada was grown using hydroponics. Indoor grow operations still rely mostly on soil based organic cultivation… "

  3. " the majority of marihuana is imported.. "

  4. " There is no reason to believe this stuff has been going south in big amounts. "

    According to the DEAland official data:

  1. Seizures of marijuana at the Mexican border are over one hundred times the volume seized at the BC border. These are the only hard numbers, everything else is conjecture.

  2. Over half of the marijuana consumed in DEAland is domestically produced.

  3. The average THC levels of marijuana in DEAland is around 3.5%, roughly where it has been for the last 20 years.

According to the Dutch government:
THC levels of marijuana grown indoors there, using the same methods, and generally the same genetics used in Canada, averages a little less than 9% THC.

I have devoted a lot of time to dealing with the prohibitionist propaganda campaign against Canadian marijuana growing.
See
Time Magazine Is Improving On The Party Line On " B. C. Bud. " Now it averages 30% THC! That is really B. S. Bud!
and

and links.
However, I think that this piece is important enough to warrant some additional attention.

First, it is one of the worst examples of why I say that the best two-word explanation of marijuana prohibition is " bad journalism. "

Second, it was published in the Boston Globe, one of the better papers in DEAland, and the Globe is now owned by the New York Times Company, so this crap -- and that is too kind a word for it – is apt to end up in the Times itself and then be distributed around the world with the Times’ imprimatur.

In short, this is a major score for the international prohibitionist propaganda apparatus that I spend so much time analyzing. Above all, it is a major degradation of journalism as a craft. Unfortunately, the Globe has been all too susceptible to this sort of thing. This is their second Reefer Madness award.)

April 26, 2000
From The Boston Globe
letter@globe.com
http://extranet.globe.com/LettersEditor/default.asp

By Colin Nickerson, Globe Staff
A NORTHERN BORDER MENACE
(MarijuanaNews note: Headlines are usually not written by the reporter, but this is in keeping with the wretched level of sensationalism in the article.)
See
Run For Your Lives! " US Says Drugs, Terror Pouring In From Canada "!
Or, The Problems Of Living Next To A Superpower Run By Narcs.

Boom in marijuana trafficking mars Canada's image

WINNIPEG, Manitoba - License plates proclaim this ''Friendly Manitoba,'' and the province is best known for wheat farms, flatness, and the rectitude of its inhabitants. But the hottest agricultural commodity flowing from the Canadian heartland these days is pot to blast your socks off.

''Manitoba product has a following as far away as south Florida,'' said Brent Eaton, special agent with US Drug Enforcement Administration's Miami office. ''On a larger scale, Canadian homegrown is displacing brands from Colombia and Mexico because of its extreme potency.''
(MarijuanaNews note: What nonsense. People in Florida would not know Manitoba from Manischevitz.

It is the nature of contraband markets that it is very difficult for the purchaser to know where the product really comes from. In any case, it would be very unlikely for Manitoba weed to transported all the way to Florida. After all, Quebec produces excellent marijuana, as does Florida itself. If there really is any Manitoba weed in Florida, it would be such a minuscule part of the market as to be irrelevant. This is just the DEA pushing the party line.)

See
Edmonton Police Actually Claim That Canadian Marijuana Is Being Exported To Mexico –
If You Believe That…

Manitoba is joining British Columbia and Quebec as producer of hydroponic weed so powerful that drug enforcement officials on both sides of border claim it no longer should be considered a soft drug.
(MarijuanaNews note: The Globe should bill the DEA for this man’s salary. This is not reporting. It is parroting. More potent marijuana is not more dangerous. On the contrary, it may well be safer. First, remember that the IOM’s only object to medical marijuana was the putative risk in smoking.
See
Column By Authors of the IOM Report On Medical Marijuana
Shows Why The Public Does Not Trust The Medical Establishment –
And Why They Should Not! With Analysis by Richard Cowan
Second, Marinol, pure THC, is an FDA approved drug, and is now on Schedule 3.)
See
Marinol Was The First Schedule 2 Drug To Be " Down-Scheduled, "
Boasts Roxanne On Its New Marinol.com Web Site.
Doesn’t That Mean That It Should Never Have Been Schedule 2 Anyway?
and links

''This isn't the stuff you smoked in college,'' said Staff Sergeant Chuck Doucette, a drug investigator with the Royal Canadian Mounted Police, which has been frustrated in its efforts to crack down on one of North America's fastest-growing crime sectors by courts so lenient that Canada is winning an international reputation as safe haven for pot purveyors.
(MarijuanaNews note: Doucette is a Vancouver nark, and I am yet to hear him tell the truth about anything. In other words, he is perfectly qualified for his job.)
See
Marijuana Prohibition And Potency, Price, And Safety --
" Is Marijuana Stronger Than It Was Back In the '60s, When Everyone Thought It Was Harmless? "
Analysis By Richard Cowan

''This is high-powered product that's producing hundreds of millions of dollars in profits for some very nasty characters,'' Doucette said. ''Most of it is going straight to the United States market.''
(MarijuanaNews note: According to Sgt. Dave Roach, a drug agent with the Royal Canadian Mounted Police in Manitoba, " The story has gotten way out of hand, " he said. " There is no reason to believe this stuff has been going south in big amounts. "

See the story immediately below. It completely undermines the premise of this garbage.)

Made-in-Canada marijuana - some of it brazenly marketed over the Internet - is also changing the definition of ''homegrown.'' Once the term conjured over-the-hill hippies tending backyard plots. Today it means indoor hydroponic ''grow-ops'' run with ruthless efficiency by Asian crime syndicates or white biker gangs, most notoriously the Hells Angels.

So much Canadian marijuana is now pouring over the border, with American enforcement agencies reporting a tenfold increase over the last two years, that the US State Department considered placing Canada on its narcotics ''black list'' - alongside the likes of Burma and Afghanistan - for not doing enough to curb the drug trade.
(MarijuanaNews note: That is nonsense.)
See
Someone Floats A Rumor That DEAland Wants To Blacklist Canada;
Washington Denies Everything, But Canadian Prohibitionists Seem To Cheer,
Sort Of… 3 Articles

The unprecedented proposal faltered under diplomatic pressure and pleas from Ottawa.

But Canada's lax attitude toward marijuana, long a source of irritation for police, is coming under fire even from the United Nations - the body's International Narcotics Control Board recently warned Canadian-based Web sites now represent the world's No. 1 Internet source of marijuana seeds and high-tech cultivation equipment, including computer-driven hydroponic systems.
See
UN Narcs Complain That Canadian Web Sites And B.C. Marijuana
Are Contributing To The " Cannabis Problem " – Interesting Article In The National Post

Hydroponics is a catch-all term for intensive indoor growing methods using heavily fertilized water, powerful lights, high heat, and humidity. Increasingly, sophisticated plant genetics also are coming into play.
(MarijuanaNews note: The " high heat and humidity " are simply undesirable side-effects of bright lights and water in an enclosed space. They are not " used " but rather counteracted by coolers, ventilation and dehumidifiers. This man knows absolutely nothing about the subject.)

The result is marijuana far more potent than anything grown out-of-doors. Levels of tetrahydrocannabinol, or THC - the compound that gives pot its pow - average 15 to 20 percent in the standard hydroponic marijuana that is already British Columbia's single most valuable agricultural product. Ultra strains top out at mind-numbing THC levels of 30 percent.
(MarijuanaNews note: The only thing mind-numbing here is this degradation of journalism.)

By contrast, the marijuana produced in Latin America, long considered creme de la creme, has an average THC content of only 6 percent and even Jamaica's strongest rarely reaches 12 percent.

(MarijuanaNews note: " The marijuana produced in Latin America, " HAS NOT BEEN " long considered creme de la crème " for decades. That honor goes to domestically produced marijuana from California and Hawaii, and indoor marijuana from almost anywhere. )

The stuff smoked by most casual American users has THC levels of 2 to 3 percent.
(MarijuanaNews note: Something close to a fact! Wow!)
See
Potent Pot Myth Undermined By Report From The Ultimate Authority. Cited By Swedish Prohibitionist Who Don’t Seem To Understand. As Usual.

''BC pot, Manitoba pot - these are getting the top dollar in the US,'' said Marc Emery, a British Columbia marijuana activist, publisher of Cannabis Culture magazine and open seller of marijuana seeds via his company, Emery Seeds of Vancouver. ''Canadian growers have a lot of skill.''
(MarijuanaNews note: This reporter never talked to Marc Emery.

In stead, he has simply taken a couple of sentences out of context from an interview in another paper. That is consistent with his lack of journalistic ethics.)
See
Marc Emery Gets A Favorable Story In The Toronto Star; A Picture of the End Of Marijuana Prohibition

Gangs employ specialist hydroponic technicians to oversee hundreds of plants at a time. A single superhybrid can yield a pound of potent buds and leaves every 90 days - worth $2,000 in Canada, $4,000 in the United States.


(MarijuanaNews note: This is complete and total BS. It is not even close to being accurate. Indoor growers, hydroponic or not, grow large numbers of small plants that yield only one quarter to one half ounce per plant! If the reported had asked Marc about this, in stead of faking an interview, he would know better, but then Marc would have corrected his other errors and there would not have been a story here.)

Canada's burgeoning marijuana industry in some ways represents a replay of the Roaring Twenties, when whiskey smuggled from north of the border slaked America's Prohibition thirst.
(MarijuanaNews note: Notice that the word " Prohibition " is used but only in conjunction with alcohol. The term " marijuana prohibition " is not allowed. Of course, all of the real problems he is writing about are precisely the result of marijuana prohibition, not marijuana.)

Then, as now, the border is simply too long and porous to deter serious smugglers - who either use crossings in remote areas or simply play the odds and place shipments in truck containers or automobile trunks, knowing that only a tiny percentage of travelers are searched.

But Canadian police are stepping up the battle on the home front, alarmed at the takeover of the industry by organized crime and soaring numbers of shootings, bombings, and other attacks. So lucrative is the enterprise that producers purchase suburban houses or urban duplexes to grow marijuana for a year or two, then abandon structures rotted by humidity and rank with mildew.
(MarijuanaNews note: This is vicious crap.

First, the marijuana growing business is a huge cottage industry. After all, the police say that there are ten thousand grow ops in BC alone. Of course, they don’t really know, but in any case it is far too large to be controlled by " organized crime. "
See
Organized Crime In The Marijuana Trade.
Why More " Law Enforcement " is Counterproductive.
An Excellent Halifax Editorial Says, " Marijuana laws encourage crime. "

Second, there is not a lot of violence associated with marijuana growing, except by Canadian standards. There certainly have not been a " soaring numbers of shootings, bombings... " There have been a number of " home invasions " – but that is what the police do when they raid a grow op.

Third, only a totally inept grower would have a house that was " rotted by humidity and rank with mildew. " If anyone really knows what they are doing, they will control the humidity to prevent the plants from molding, thereby ruining its market value.)

In an especially troubling trend, criminals now routinely hire ''front families,'' often illegal immigrants from Vietnam or China, to lend an outwardly normal appearance to dwellings serving as hydroponic pot farms.
See
The Racist Origins Of Canada’s Marijuana Prohibition Reported In the National Post.

''They want kids playing on the lawn, mom smiling from the window to defer suspicions of neighbors,'' said Doucette. ''But these places are often firetraps, full of makeshift wiring, propane tanks, chemicals.''
(MarijuanaNews note: Wait a minute. First we are told that these are very " sophisticated " operations. Then we are told that they are firetraps. Of course, the " chemicals " are just various fertilizers of the sort that any gardener would have. Propane is sometimes burned to create carbon dioxide, but there are several million farm houses and house trailers that have propane heating. Propane is actually very safe. In any case, there have not been any major problems with it.)

In recent weeks, Winnipeg police have raided eight substantial indoor hydroponic operations, seizing $1.7 million worth of marijuana plants. ''It's a huge cash business,'' said Detective Sergeant Ron Trakalo of the Winnipeg Police Vice Squad. ''It's a crime industry literally growing up all around us.''
See
Canadian Police Lie to The Canadian Media Who Lie To Their Readers
To Justify More Power Over the Canadian People To Please DEAland Narks
An Utterly Wretched Piece Of Pseudo-journalism

The busts in Manitoba produced a flurry of headlines, mainly because the staid province seemed such an unlikely marijuana producing center. In fact, the province is still a long way from catching up with Canada's reigning champs, British Columbia and Quebec - nonetheless, among aficionados, BC Bud and Quebec Gold have been joined by Winnipeg Wheelchair Weed, so-nicknamed because of its disabling effects on users.
(MarijuanaNews note: Disabling effects?? It is more likely to get someone out of a wheelchair than to put someone in one.)
See
Medical Marijuana Got Man Out Of Wheelchair;
" Meanwhile, the MS Society of Canada keeps a cautious distance... "

In British Columbia, annual marijuana cultivation is reckoned to be worth more than $2 billion, making the illicit plant one of the most important sectors of the provincial economy. ''As an industry, pot comes just after logging and mining,'' said Sergeant Randa Elliott of the Organized Crime Agency. ''We estimate there are 10,000 grow-ops in the province. ''

In raids last month, the agency, composed of Royal Canadian Mounted Police officers and local British Columbia police, swooped down on 80 operations, seizing 14,258 marijuana plants with an estimated value of $5.6 million, hundreds of pounds of marijuana packaged for shipment, and - rare for Canada - an array of firearms.
(MarijuanaNews note: That is an average of only 178 plants per raid, which would include seedlings, males, etc. That does not sound like many are major " sophisticated " operations.)

''One home was heavily fortified with steel doors, alarm systems, and surveillance cameras,'' Elliott said. ''Obviously we're not talking Ma and Pa growing just enough good stuff to stay mellow. We're talking major crime.''
(MarijuanaNews note: One place has standard Boston – albeit not Canadian -- home security, so that proves that " we are talking about major crime. " By what definition? That is as illogical as everything else here.)

The emergence of Canadian marijuana as an important export crop reflects a transformation in the cultivation of North America's favorite recreational drug.
See
A Very Interesting Article In The Toronto Sun Looks Calmly At The Huge Canadian Marijuana Business

Surreptitious clearings in remote rural areas have been around for decades, of course, but cultivation in Canada was restricted by the short growing season. And the potency of northern weed was unremarkable.
(MarijuanaNews note: That again is simply not true. Marijuana grows well in the far north and outdoor BC Bud is excellent. This is truly fact free journalism. Once again, if he had just talked to Marc Emery, or anyone who isn’t a nark, then he would have known that that statement is completely false.)

Now, the rural plots have been overshadowed by hydroponic groweries requiring little space and producing powerful product. Such operations are expanding rapidly in the United States, too, but Canada is winning a reputation as a safe base because courts treat even commercial cultivation as a minor offense, rarely handing out jail time or fines of more than $2,000.
(MarijuanaNews note: Excuse me, but if " such operations are expanding rapidly in the United States, too, " -- and they are, except that, as in Canada, most are not hydroponic -- then what is the deterrent value of harsher penalties? Once again: According to the DEA, half of all the marijuana consumed in DEAland is domestically grown, so outrageous penalties clearly do not stop cultivation.)

''That's not a penalty for a pot grower pocketing $200,000 per crop,'' griped one drug enforcement officer in Quebec. ''That's a minor business expense, a cheap license fee. It's a national embarrassment.''
(MarijuanaNews note: No, it is the party line that is " a national embarrassment.''

Remember that the average grow busted was only 178 plants. Even if all of them were mature females, the value of the crop would be around C$11,000 or US$7,500.

That is, with half an ounce per plant, a very generous assumption, times 180 plants = 90 ounces divided by 16 ounces per pound = 5.5 pounds at C$2,000 per pound. And that is gross, every 90 days or so. From that a person must deduct expenses and calculate the value of the grower's time. It is a good living, but that is all that most people get out of it, if they don't get robbed, arrested, or lose their crop to other problems.)

April 10, 2000
From The Grand Forks Herald
http://www.northscape.com/
letters@gfherald.com
By Tom Bryan, Herald Staff Writer

POTENT CANADIAN POT IS MOVING INTO N.D.

Porous Border Opens Door For Drug Trade; Quantity Disputed

Drug agents in North Dakota believe potent marijuana grown in high-tech underground laboratories in Manitoba is filtering into the United States through porous international border crossings.

Marijuana growers are building sophisticated below-ground bunkers all over rural Winnipeg, said Sgt. Lyle MacMillan, a Winnipeg Police drug agent. Some of the operations are growing hundreds -- maybe thousands - -- of marijuana plants that produce three to four crops a year.

Jerry Kemmet, who heads the North Dakota Bureau of Criminal Investigation, said the lightly guarded border between Manitoba and North Dakota provides easy routes for traffickers to move the pot south.

" The border is so open, " Kemmet said. " There are some crossings where all they do is set up (pylon) cones at night to stop traffic. "

High THC Factor

The Canadian marijuana has a THC level 30 to 40 percent higher than traditional marijuana grown in Mexico and South America, officials said.

THC -- short for tetrahydrocannabinol -- is the chemical produced in the buds of a marijuana plant that produces an intoxicating sensation when smoked or ingested.

" This is some of the best marijuana in the nation, " Kemmet said. " It is tremendously potent. "

Kemmet said there is no proof the Canadian pot is coming to North Dakota in large quantities, but he's concerned about the influx of the plant because it's such a potent strain. Simply stated: It's a better-quality product -- and pot smokers know it, he said.

Exaggerated?

Sgt. Dave Roach, a drug agent with the Royal Canadian Mounted Police in Manitoba, said the problem is not as bad as people think.

" The story has gotten way out of hand, " he said. " There is no reason to believe this stuff has been going south in big amounts. "
(MarijuanaNews note: The purpose of an ideology is to keep everyone on the party line. This was a major lapse, but it had no impact on the pseudojournalism being perpetrated. It was ignored by the Globe, and notice that the next sentence in this article is argumentative. "

But Roach admitted that a lot of high-grade marijuana is, in fact, being grown in Manitoba.

" They're growing this stuff in James Bond-type bunkers, " he said. " We could fly our planes over an operation and never know they're down there. "

Roach said the pot-growing operations around Winnipeg have probably existed for years, but have become more commonplace in the last three years.

Part of the problem, MacMillan said, is the light jail sentences pot growers receive in Manitoba. He said most growers are charged with " producing marijuana " or " possession of marijuana for the purpose of delivering. "

" The penalties are next to nothing, " he said. " If it's their first offense, they usually just get fined.
